# Redlich-Kwong fugacity coefficient and departure functions

`eos.rk_departure`

## Equation

$$
\psi = -\frac{1}{2}, \qquad I = \ln\frac{z + B}{z}, \qquad C = \frac{A}{B}, \qquad \ln\varphi = z - 1 - \ln\left(z - B\right) - CI, \qquad \frac{H^{R}}{RT} = \left(z - 1\right) + C\left(\psi - 1\right)I, \qquad \frac{S^{R}}{R} = \ln\left(z - B\right) + C\psi I
$$

In the form the library evaluates:

```python
psi = -1/2
I = ln((z + b_reduced)/z)
c = a_reduced/b_reduced
ln_phi = z - 1 - ln(z - b_reduced) - c*I
h_dep_rt = (z - 1) + c*(psi - 1)*I
s_dep_r = ln(z - b_reduced) + c*psi*I

```

## Source

**Redlich, O.; Kwong, J. N. S. (1949)**

On the Thermodynamics of Solutions. V. Chemical Reviews, 44(1), 233-244

DOI: [10.1021/cr60137a013](https://doi.org/10.1021/cr60137a013)

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a_reduced` | dimensionless | the cubic's attraction parameter `A`, from `eos.rk_alpha_ab` |
| `b_reduced` | dimensionless | the cubic's repulsion parameter `B`, from `eos.rk_alpha_ab` |
| `z` | dimensionless | The compressibility factor, from the cubic. This calc does not check that `z` is a root of the cubic `A` and `B` define. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ln_phi` | dimensionless | The logarithm of the fugacity coefficient. |
| `h_dep_rt` | dimensionless | The departure enthalpy divided by `R*T`. |
| `s_dep_r` | dimensionless | the departure entropy divided by `R` |
| `cp_dep_r` | dimensionless | The departure heat capacity divided by `R`. |


## Valid range

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `b_reduced > 0` | raises | `b_reduced` appears as a divisor in the coefficient `A/B`, and at B = 0 the departure functions are zero - the ideal-gas limit, which is not reachable by division. |
| `z_minus_b_reduced > 0` | raises | `z` appears as `ln(z - b_reduced)`, so `z = b_reduced` is the zero-volume limit and `z < b_reduced` makes the logarithm of a negative number. |


## Assumptions

These are **not** checked at runtime. They are what the caller has to
satisfy for the result to mean what it says.


- **`z` is a root of the cubic that `a_reduced` and `b_reduced` define.** NOT CHECKED here, and not checkable: it would mean solving the cubic.

- the departure functions are relative to the ideal-gas state at the same temperature and pressure.

- no mixing rule is applied. These are pure-component departure functions, computed from the composition-weighted `A` and `B` a caller passes.

- the alpha derivative `psi` is the constant `-1/2` - RK's `1/sqrt(Tr)` has no fitted coefficient, so `psi` and `T*dpsi/dT` are constants and this calc takes neither `kappa` nor `Tr`.




## Worked example

Source: derived from the equations above

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| `a_reduced` | 0.1866943088347048 |
| `b_reduced` | 0.02707510936404929 |
| `z` | 0.8119920001727409 |

| Output | Expected |
|---|---|
| `ln_phi` | -0.17200180559684855 |
| `h_dep_rt` | -0.5272648660603503 |
| `s_dep_r` | -0.3552630604635018 |
| `cp_dep_r` | 1.2455752814017873 |

Relative tolerance: `1e-12`

The vapour root of the propane-like state in this namespace: A = 0.1866943088347048 from eos.rk_alpha_ab at Tr = 0.8, Pr = 0.25 B = 0.02707510936404929 from the same call z = 0.8119920001727409 the larger admissible root psi = -1/2 I = ln((z + B)/z) = ln(0.8390671095367901 / 0.8119920001727409) = 0.03281681856870471 C = A/B = 0.1866943088347048 / 0.02707510936404929 = 6.895440705963152 z - B = 0.7849168908086916, ln(z - B) = -0.2422426534574107 And the outputs: ln_phi = z - 1 - ln(z - B) - C*I = -0.17200180559684855 h_dep_rt = (z - 1) + C*(psi - 1)*I = -0.5272648660603503 s_dep_r = ln(z - B) + C*psi*I = -0.3552630604635018 The identity closes: h_dep_rt - s_dep_r = -0.1720018055968485 against ln_phi = -0.17200180559684855.
